the factors influencing mineral availability are (1) the intensity of use, (2) the growth rate of demand, (3) the lifetime of reserves, (4) the relative importance of centres, and (5) the lead time to development.
the lifetime of a mineral resource is a key factor for the short-term mineral supply and the lead time to mine is a crucial factor for the long-term supply.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the short-term mineral supply of commodities is determined by the intensity of use and the growth rate, whereas the long-term mineral supply of the commodities is controlled by the lifetime of reserves.
the future supply of mineral commodities is determined by geological factors, the growth rate of mineral consumption and the lead time to mineral production.

the short-term availability of a mineral commodity is controlled mainly by the intensity of use and the growth rate in consumption, whereas the long-term availability is controlled mainly by geological factors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the future mineral supply will depend on the interaction of geological factors (reserves and resources, production centres and depletion of resources) with the demand for mineral commodities (growth rate of consumption, intensity-of-use factors).
the factors influencing mineral-commodity supply are mainly geological, and that the geological factors are the most important ones.
the future mineral supply will mainly depend on the geological characteristics of the resource base and the technical development of the mining industry.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the intensity-of-use factor is the most important factor for predicting mineral-commodity supply.
the analysis of the above factors can provide an indication of the availability and the future short-term and long-term trends in mineral supply.
the factors influencing future mineral-commodity trends should be considered in a comprehensive way and not individually.
